title: Lightweight remote moderation notes — Rollout & routing policy probe
summary: Notes from a lightweight, remote-moderated UX probe focused on the model rollout and smart-routing policy edit flows. Objective: validate whether engineers and platform owners can create, preview, and roll back routing policies with confidence in a single contextual surface without leaving the rollout page. Sessions were short (30–40 minutes), high-frequency, and intentionally informal to surface friction quickly.
sessions: 5 moderated remote sessions (30–40m each) with product, onboarding, and two customer platform engineers
Tasks given: 1) create a new routing policy that routes 20% traffic to a quantized variant, 2) preview deterministic fallback when region capacity limited, 3) create a canary rollout and then abort
Environment: interactive wireframe (Figma prototype), console logs stubbed, a simplified policy DSL shown inline
Participants: mid-senior ML infra engineers (3), product platform manager (1), SRE for a customer (1)
raw_observations: Participants liked inline preview but wanted clearer signal when a policy would actually take effect (hover vs save ambiguity).
Several participants attempted to copy an existing policy via URL; expected 'duplicate' action on the policy card rather than start from scratch.
The fallback preview modal showed simulated latency numbers but users questioned the assumptions and wanted source info (region, instance type).
The canary weight slider was useful but lacked keyboard accessibility; two participants tried arrow keys and were confused.
Users expected an audit trail immediately visible on the rollout card (who changed, when, and a one-click rollback).
Some confusion around terminology: 'variant' vs 'model variant' vs 'model variant profile' — participants used these interchangeably and asked for inline definitions.
user_quotes: I want to see exactly when this routing rule becomes active — not just 'saved' but 'live'—otherwise I won't trust it.
Copy policy? I would duplicate the card and edit it. I wouldn't go to a flow that feels like making a new thing from zero.
The preview numbers are neat but I need to know what hardware you're assuming — that changes the latency expectations a lot.
If rollback is two clicks away, I'm not confident to try canary in production. Show me the rollback path first.
ux_issues: Ambiguous save vs apply state for routing policies — no explicit 'go live' confirmation.
Insufficient provenance in the preview simulation (missing region/hardware assumptions).
No quick duplicate action on policy cards — forced re-entry increases error rate and time.
Canary controls not fully keyboard accessible and slider lacks incremental input box.
Audit/rollback controls buried on the detail page rather than on the rollout overview card.
Terminology inconsistency across console surfaces leading to cognitive friction.
prioritization_rationale: High: explicit apply/activate affordance — users will not use canaries without clear live state (security & trust risk).
High: quick duplicate action — small engineering effort, large time savings across several support tickets.
Medium: surface hardware/region assumptions in preview — improves trust but may need infra integration.
Medium: keyboard/accessibility fixes for slider — low effort, required for accessibility compliance.
Low: glossary and microcopy rewrite — valuable but can be staged after core affordances are addressed.
wireframe-notes: Introduce an 'Apply policy' CTA that is distinct from 'Save draft' — visual emphasis and color change; tooltip explains difference.
Add a small provenance chip in the preview header: 'Simulated on: us-west2, p4d; token: 512' — clicking opens detailed assumptions.
Policy card with overflow menu: Duplicate, Export JSON, View History. Duplicate should prefill the new policy modal.
Canary control: slider + numeric input + keyboard arrows + confirm modal that shows expected token throughput at selected weight.
Rollout card to include a one-click 'Rollback to previous' with a safety modal and inline changelog snippet.
design-decisions: Prefer explicit apply step to reduce accidental live policy changes — will be gated by role-based permission checks.
Keep preview simulation lightweight; link to a detailed simulation page for power users instead of embedding complex controls in the small modal.
Expose duplicate/export to reduce manual re-entry and enable offline editing via JSON export.
Accessibility: add keyboard support for all micro-controls; reuse existing accessible slider component from console library.
backlog-actions: PROD-1912: Add 'Apply policy' CTA + save state machine on policy editor
PROD-1913: Policy card menu — add Duplicate and View History actions
INF-2348: Surface simulation assumptions from serving runtime (region, instance family) into preview modal
UX-1207: Accessibility fixes for canary slider (keyboard, numeric input)
DOC-882: Microcopy glossary for variant/model terminology on rollout surfaces
next_steps: Prioritize PROD-1912 and UX-1207 for next sprint; aim for a lightweight shipping increment that toggles the apply flow on a feature flag.
Schedule a 60-minute follow-up with two customer platform engineers to validate the 'duplicate' affordance in a clickable prototype (target week of 2026-08-30).
Estimate effort for INF-2348 with infra team to determine if preview assumptions can be surfaced via existing telemetry endpoints.
Draft microcopy glossary and run a quick hallway test with three engineers to confirm terminology fixes.
